inv-scalar-int::investigations/scalar-int/scalar-runtime.test.ts::[observation] silent wrong integer quotient on the GPU through the f32 path (quantified) INT_MIN / -1 and large quotients saturate: T(a / b) i32 gives 2147483520 (largest f32 below 2^31), WGSL integer division would give INT_MIN::status

inv-scalar-int::investigations/scalar-int/scalar-runtime.test.ts::[PROBABLE DEFECT S3] u32 bitwise results on the CPU are signed int32 (negative when bit 31 is set) [observation] realistic impact: an xorshift32 hash written with `^`, `<<`, `>>>` (pattern used by the repo examples) is congruent on CPU and GPU, but d.f32(h) / 2^32 is negative on the CPU for about half of the seeds::status

inv-scalar-int::investigations/scalar-int/scalar-runtime.test.ts::[PROBABLE DEFECT S3] u32 bitwise results on the CPU are signed int32 (negative when bit 31 is set) [observation] same ops on i32 agree exactly on CPU and GPU::status

inv-scalar-int::investigations/scalar-int/scalar-runtime.test.ts::[PROBABLE DEFECT S3] u32 bitwise results on the CPU are signed int32 (negative when bit 31 is set) [TypeGPU] u32 `>>` is deprecated in favour of `>>>` (CPU `>>` is an arithmetic shift: wrong value, not only wrong range); `>>>` matches the GPU::status

inv-vector-fns::investigations/vector-fns/const-fold.test.ts::targeted constant-expression cases [observation] length/normalize of ordinary-looking vectors: the baked constant is the mathematical value, the runtime GPU overflows/underflows (const != runtime)::value

inv-vector-fns::investigations/vector-fns/const-fold.test.ts::targeted constant-expression cases [WGSL] constant overflow is a shader-creation error: length(vec3f(3e38)) = 5.2e38 baked from the f64 CPU value is rejected loudly (not silently inf)::status

inv-vector-fns::investigations/vector-fns/const-fold.test.ts::targeted constant-expression cases [TypeGPU] normalize(vec3f(0)) as a constant: loud resolve error (CPU would produce NaN); runtime GPU gives NaN::status
inv-vector-fns::investigations/vector-fns/const-fold.test.ts::targeted constant-expression cases [observation] atan2(y, x) constants at x=-0 / origin: baked IEEE value vs the runtime GPU quirk::value

inv-vector-fns::investigations/vector-fns/const-fold.test.ts::targeted constant-expression cases [observation] smoothstep(e, e, x) as constants: TypeGPU bakes 0 (no shader-creation error as the raw WGSL rule would give)::value

inv-vector-fns::investigations/vector-fns/const-fold.test.ts::targeted constant-expression cases [API limitation] round(vec) / trunc / faceForward / refract with constant arguments are NOT folded (emitted as WGSL calls) and still compute correctly::value
inv-vector-fns::investigations/vector-fns/const-fold.test.ts::targeted constant-expression cases [observation] round(2.5)/round(-2.5) folded scalar constants use ties-to-even like the GPU::value

inv-vector-fns::investigations/vector-fns/edge-cases.test.ts::round: ties to even [WGSL], and the sign of zero [WGSL] GPU round = round-half-even for every tie / near-tie (scalar and vec3f lanes); [TypeGPU] scalar CPU agrees::status

inv-vector-fns::investigations/vector-fns/edge-cases.test.ts::round: ties to even [WGSL], and the sign of zero [observation] sign of zero: round(-0.5) is -0 on the GPU and +0 on the CPU; sign(-0) is -0 on the CPU and +0 on the GPU (WGSL allows ignoring the sign of zero)::value
inv-vector-fns::investigations/vector-fns/edge-cases.test.ts::clamp / smoothstep / step edges [WGSL] smoothstep with edge0 > edge1 descends (CPU and GPU), and values are in [0,1]::status

inv-vector-fns::investigations/vector-fns/edge-cases.test.ts::clamp / smoothstep / step edges [observation] smoothstep(e, e, x) (indeterminate in WGSL for runtime args): CPU returns 0 always, GPU returns 1 for x > e (known harmless divergence)::value
inv-vector-fns::investigations/vector-fns/edge-cases.test.ts::clamp / smoothstep / step edges [WGSL] step: edge <= x -> 1 (equal gives 1; signed zeros equal; 0.99999994 < 1)::status

inv-vector-fns::investigations/vector-fns/edge-cases.test.ts::overflow / underflow of intermediates (length, normalize, distance, dot, mix, fma) [observation: expected difference] length(vec3f) / normalize: the CPU (f64 intermediates) gives the mathematical value, the GPU overflows or underflows in the squares::value

inv-vector-fns::investigations/vector-fns/edge-cases.test.ts::overflow / underflow of intermediates (length, normalize, distance, dot, mix, fma) [observation: expected difference] [observation] dot / distance / fma / mix intermediates: GPU inf where the exact result is finite (cancellation after overflow)::value

inv-vector-fns::investigations/vector-fns/edge-cases.test.ts::overflow / underflow of intermediates (length, normalize, distance, dot, mix, fma) [observation: expected difference] [TypeGPU] normalize(vec3f(0)): the CPU throws (NaN is not representable in vec3f), the GPU returns NaN lanes (indeterminate: zero vector is outside the domain)::status

inv-vector-fns::investigations/vector-fns/edge-cases.test.ts::atan2 and zero arguments [observation] atan2(y, x) with x = +-0 and the origin: CPU follows IEEE/JS, the GPU does not (WGSL: error unbounded at the origin / tiny |x|)::value
inv-vector-fns::investigations/vector-fns/edge-cases.test.ts::mix with t outside [0,1] and extreme t [WGSL: x*(1-z)+y*z] [WGSL] extrapolation and exactness of the formula::status

inv-vector-fns::investigations/vector-fns/edge-cases.test.ts::fract of negative and large numbers [WGSL: x - floor(x)] [WGSL] fract matches the f32 x - floor(x) (tiny negatives round to 1.0, allowed by the spec note)::status

inv-vector-fns::investigations/vector-fns/edge-cases.test.ts::sinh for small arguments [WGSL: inherited from (exp(x) - exp(-x)) * 0.5] [WGSL] GPU sinh stays within the absolute bound implied by the exp-based formula; [observation] relative error is huge for |x| < ~1e-4 while the CPU (Math.sinh) is accurate::status
